title: REPLACEMENT OF TURN SIGNAL AND HAZARD WARNING SWITCH

content.text: REPLACEMENT OF TURN SIGNAL AND HAZARD WARNING SWITCH
REPLACE TURN SIGNAL AND HAZARD WARNING SWITCH

content.description: Exploded view of turn signal and hazard warning switch assembly showing the switch unit being removed from the steering column

items: (a) Remove the terminals from the connector. (See page BE-2)
(b) Remove the turn signal and hazard switch.
(c) Install the turn signal and hazard switch.
(d) Connect the terminals to the connector. (See pages BE-3 and 18)

content.description: Turn signal flasher connector showing 3-terminal configuration with terminals numbered 1, 2, and 3

items: (a) Connect the positive (+) lead from the battery to terminal 3. Connect the negative (−) lead to terminal 2 and R.
(b) Connect a 55W bulb between terminals 1 and 2, and check that the bulb goes on and off.

content.description: Test circuit diagram showing battery connected to flasher unit with 55W test bulb

content.text:
NOTE: The turn signal lights should flash 75 to 95 times per minute.
If one of the front or rear turn signal lights has an open circuit, the number of flashes will be more than 120 per minute.
If one of the side turn signal lights has an open circuit, the number of flashes will increase by about 10 per minute.
If operation is not as specified, replace the flasher.

content.description: Fade-out relay connector diagram showing 6 terminals with test bulb connection points

content.text: Connect the positive (+) lead from the battery to terminal 2. Connect the negative (−) lead to terminals 1 and 6. Connect a 3.4W test bulb between terminals 2 and 4.

items: (b) Disconnect the negative (−) lead from terminal 1, and check that the bulb fades out about 8.5 seconds later.

content.text: If operation is not as specified, replace the relay.
2. INSPECT OUTSIDE HANDLE SWITCH CIRCUIT OPERATION

content.description: Alternative fade-out relay test circuit showing battery connection to terminals 2, 3, 4, and 6 with test bulb

content.text: Connect the positive (+) lead from battery to terminal 2. Connect the negative (−) lead to terminals 3 and 6. Connect a 3.4 W test bulb between terminals 2 and 4.
Disconnect the negative (−) lead from terminal 3, and check that the bulb fades out about 8.5 seconds later.
If operation is not as specified, replace the relay.
